newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open slightly weaker with U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open slightly weaker with U.S. market.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly weaker with softer U.S. treasuries on Thursday, but maintained recent spread narrowing gains against the U.S. yield curve, analysts said.

"You have to be impressed with how well the (Canadian) market is holding in," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed income with First Marathon Securities Ltd. "Watching the U.S. market is very critical here after yesterday's wave of selling."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.15 to C$111.85 to yield 7.004 percent.

The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.97 percent. The spread between the bonds was three basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close. Three basis points is the lowest the spread between the two bonds has been this decade.

"I think someone is going to try to drive that long Canada-U.S. spread negative today," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "Technically we are on the brink of breaking out on the long bond. Technicals are very, very positive for Canada."
Despite a slight fall in prices, Dong said the Canadian market was well bid this morning.
In new issue news, the Bank of Canada will release details this afternoon of the Government of Canada's auction of five-year bonds on May 28. Auction details will be released at 1530 EDT/1930 GMT.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.08 to C$103.80 to yield 6.453 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.73 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds was 28 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.94 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.13 percent.
